lessons.lesson: Never dispatch the independent checker before the maker's evidence artifacts are sealed on disk; a FAIL caused by sequencing is a maker defect, not a product defect, and it costs a full checker round.
lessons.rule: seal evidence -> commit -> then dispatch the checker; the checker brief must name the canonical path of every artifact it will read.

lessons.lesson: A lane sandbox can silently invalidate a checker's runtime re-execution (git subprocess, site-packages read, --basetemp delete) and produce FAIL verdicts that look like product failures.
lessons.rule: put the candidate worktree and a lane-owned venv inside a trusted root, use a fresh --basetemp path per run, and read the raw tool output before believing a FAIL.

lessons.lesson: The lane pool's transport_model vocabulary decides which model id the relay will actually serve; a qualified provider/model string can be rejected with HTTP 400 'Model is unavailable' even though the same model id works bare.
lessons.rule: probe the arm with a nonce before relying on it, and record the served arm (provider/model/usage status) in the receipt; never assume the committed pool will serve the intended arm.

lessons.lesson: A verifier that reports PASS while noting it could not see the evidence text is a weak PASS; ask for the literal summary line to be captured into a file inside the checker's own scratch.
lessons.rule: require the checker to write its raw command output to a file and quote the exact summary line; that closes the disclosure instead of leaving it open.

lessons.lesson: Wheels are not byte-reproducible across build directories, so a digest only binds to a specific artifact.
lessons.rule: store the exact artifact in-repo next to the evidence and bind the digest to that path.

iteration_outcome: the round closed on checker PASS_WITH_DISCLOSURES + 15/15 self-check with 0 fabricated PASS and 0 product defects surfaced by the independent principal
evolution_ceiling: local, scoped, single-round evidence only; no SWOF W3 effect, no Host acceptance, no full-contract closure
